result.summary: The image shows a residential street with sidewalks on both sides but a complete lack of marked pedestrian crossing infrastructure at the visible intersection. The wide, unmarked roadway and presence of parked cars near corners create potential visibility and safety issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected path.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or traffic signals are visible to regulate vehicle movement at the junction.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb may block the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the corner

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the intersection.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and properly sloped ramps at all crossing points.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street intersection with brick row houses and basic pedestrian infrastructure. While sidewalks and a marked crosswalk are present, the environment lacks high-visibility markings and clear sightlines due to parked vehicles near the corner.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars near the intersection corners block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Low Visibility Crosswalk
hazards.description: The crosswalk is marked with thin transverse lines which are less visible to approaching drivers than high-visibility patterns.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the intersection to improve visibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a residential one-way street with sidewalks on both sides, though they lack ADA-compliant curb ramps and marked crosswalks at the intersection. Parked vehicles along the curb create sightline obstructions, and the sidewalk surfaces show signs of neglect with encroaching vegetation and cracking.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks, providing no designated space or priority for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the right curb can obscure pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Tripping Hazards
hazards.description: Encroaching vegetation and cracked pavement on the sidewalk create uneven surfaces for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way at the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install standardized curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces to ensure the intersection is accessible for all users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a residential street with row houses and narrow, poorly maintained sidewalks. There is a complete lack of formal crossing infrastructure at the intersection, including marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps.

hazards.name: Uneven and cracked sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk at the corner is severely cracked and uneven, posing a trip hazard.

hazards.name: Lack of curb ramps
hazards.description: There are no curb ramps at the intersection, making it inaccessible for people with mobility devices.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Trash cans and residential stairs narrow the usable pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk in front of the brick building

interventions.title: Install ADA-compliant curb ramps
interventions.description: Provide sloped transitions at the corner to ensure accessibility for all users.

interventions.description: Paint high-visibility crosswalks to define pedestrian right-of-way and improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Sidewalk repair
